column1: Colour coding is helpful in identification of gas cylinders and lines even by laymen if they are familiarized
with such Colour codes. Almost all countries follow their own guidelines but efforts have been made to
prescribe universal colour coding. British Compressed Gases Association introduced cylinder
identification and colour coding scheme through BS EN 1089 – 3 which has been harmonised in the
European Union. The colours used for medical gases are harmonised on the basis of ISO 32 standard.
The colour coding is applied to the shoulder or the curved portion of the cylinder and it identifies the
property of the gas inside the cylinder.
